final_answer: The sky appears blue during the day due to Rayleigh scattering, where shorter wavelengths (blue/violet) scatter more strongly than longer ones (red/orange). At sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere, scattering away most blue light and leaving red/orange hues to dominate. This inverse fourth-power relationship with wavelength makes blue prevalent when the path length is short, but red/orange visible when the path length is long.
